page: Amazon Web Services r9g.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton arm64 processors. The instance provides 192 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading contention across its 192 vCPUs. It is equipped with 1536 GB of system RAM, yielding a consistent 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation designed for memory-bound workloads.

Network connectivity features a 100 Gbps baseline bandwidth, facilitating high-throughput node communications and clustered data exchange. The r9g.48xlarge does not include local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage solutions such as Amazon EBS for block volumes. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are absent, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned by default.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio provides dense memory capacity per core, offering efficient resource alignment for environments that require vast memory arrays without requiring excessive over-provisioning of CPU resources. The platform is well suited for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, big data analytics engines, and high-throughput transaction processing systems.
description: Amazon Web Services r9g.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by 64-bit arm64 AWS Graviton processors under the AWS Nitro System. It is configured with 192 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz with one execution thread per core, combined with 1536 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU distribution. Network interfaces deliver a 100 Gbps baseline throughput for low-latency, high-volume distributed communication. The instance does not provide bundled local NVMe storage or discrete GPU hardware, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent data. Designed for memory-intensive enterprise infrastructure, the r9g.48xlarge supports large in-memory caches, distributed memory-bound analytics, and enterprise database systems.
